edges.label: An Air Force telescope deployment covering Air Force Western Test Range launches
edges.note: Instrument owned by the Range Measurements Laboratory of the Air Force Eastern Test Range; nine of eleven Vandenberg launches covered; the resulting film classified Top Secret on a weapons-vulnerability rationale and later destroyed.

edges.label: Coverage of Vandenberg launches from a site about 100 miles north
edges.note: The Big Sur site gave a side-look at launches into the Western Test Range that local telephoto coverage at Vandenberg could not, because of prevailing fog.

edges.label: Project engineer for the deployment
edges.note: His own opening line: 'I was the project engineer for these experiments.' He supplies the dates, the instrument, the launch name, the photographs and a contemporaneous 13 October 1964 staff study cited by title.

b.label: Kingston A. George, 'The Big Sur UFO: An Identified Flying Object', Skeptical Inquirer, Winter 1993

edges.label: Author
edges.note: He identifies himself as the project engineer in the article's opening line. Type research, not custody: he wrote it, he does not hold custody of anything.

edges.label: Published point-by-point rebuttal by the project engineer, Skeptical Inquirer, Winter 1993
edges.note: TIER 1 DESPITE BEING A DENIAL, because it is a signed article in a named journal by a participant who cites his own dated 1964 staff study, publishes photographs of the team, and concedes a point to Jacobs on lasers. He answers six numbered conclusions and states that Jacobs 'was technically not authorized to view the pictures we were collecting'.

a.label: Kingston A. George, 'The Big Sur UFO: An Identified Flying Object', Skeptical Inquirer, Winter 1993

edges.label: The project engineer's published rebuttal of the UFO reading of the event
edges.note: A directed denial by a named participant, and the model this board should want: it establishes the witness's unit, appointment, presence and debriefing while disputing what was on the film.

edges.label: Major present at the Big Sur site; Jacobs's corroborating witness
edges.note: Tier 1 for his presence, which is established by the project engineer's own published photograph caption, and Tier 2 for what he later wrote to researchers. THE BOARD HAS BEEN ATTRIBUTING HIS LETTERS TO THE WRONG MAN AND THE WRONG EVENT; see research/leads/nuclear-corrections-2026-09-19.json.

edges.label: On-site commander at the filming; his presence, unit and role confirmed by the project engineer in print
edges.note: THE ONLY TIER 1 WITNESS-TO-CASE EDGE IN THIS CLUSTER. Jacobs published his own account in January 1989; Kingston George, the project engineer, wrote in 1993 that 'Bob was named the on-site commander by the 1369th Photo Squadron and managed the logistics of the operation at the Big Sur location', and published team photographs captioning Jacobs into and out of them. The edge carries his PRESENCE, not his interpretation.

edges.label: 1369th Photographic Squadron, Vandenberg AFB, May 1963 to May 1966
edges.note: His own published statement of his post, independently confirmed as to unit and role by the project engineer.
